name: Stags' Leap Winery Cabernet Sauvignon Napa Valley 2016
text:
## Stags' Leap Winery Cabernet Sauvignon Napa Valley 2016

**Not to be confused with its neighbour.** Stags' Leap Winery (apostrophe after the s) is a different estate from its neighbour Stag's Leap Wine Cellars (apostrophe before the s). Both are in the [Stags Leap District](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stags_Leap_District_AVA) of [Napa Valley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Napa_Valley_AVA).

**The story.** Stags' Leap Winery lies near [Yountville](https://www.google.com/maps?q=Stags'+Leap+Winery,+Napa,+California,+USA&t=k). It was founded by Horace Chase with his uncle, W.W. Thompson, on land already planted with vines; they named it after a legend of a lone stag leaping over the palisades to escape hunters. The Chases built a manor house and winery, the first vintage was 1893, and by 1895 the estate was making 40,000 gallons a year; it became a social destination, famous for parties with politicians, artists and writers ([Dallas Wine Chick](https://www.dallaswinechick.com/sitting-down-with-christophe-paubert-a-winemaker-legend-from-stags-leap-winery/)).

The fortune was lost, and in 1913 Frances Grange bought the property and turned it into a working ranch and Napa's top resort. After her time it fell into disrepair until Carl Doumani restored it in 1971: he hoped to reopen the hotel, but Napa's zoning laws stopped him, so he planted grapes instead. The vineyard today is 85 acres in 23 blocks ([Dallas Wine Chick](https://www.dallaswinechick.com/sitting-down-with-christophe-paubert-a-winemaker-legend-from-stags-leap-winery/)). Beringer bought the winery in 1997, and it now belongs to [Treasury Wine Estates](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Treasury_Wine_Estates) ([Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stags'_Leap_Winery)).

**The winemaker.** Christophe Paubert, the senior winemaker, joined in 2009 from Bordeaux, with Château d'Yquem and Château Gruaud-Larose on his CV. He is modest about his role: "the wines you taste are because of the fruit, not because of anything that I do differently." The fruit is hand-picked and hand-sorted, from the estate and from partner growers in Napa and Carneros ([Dallas Wine Chick](https://www.dallaswinechick.com/sitting-down-with-christophe-paubert-a-winemaker-legend-from-stags-leap-winery/)).

**The vintage.** [Jancis Robinson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jancis_Robinson)'s [northern California vintage chart](https://www.jancisrobinson.com/learn/vintages/northern-california) describes 2016 as a year of even temperatures and a cooler September, giving wines of elegance and structure, and a strong year for Napa Cabernet.

**What the critics say for 2016.**
- **Dallas Wine Chick**, a wine blogger who tasted it with Paubert: black cherry, truffle, currant, vanilla, nutmeg and tobacco ([Dallas Wine Chick](https://www.dallaswinechick.com/sitting-down-with-christophe-paubert-a-winemaker-legend-from-stags-leap-winery/)).
- I couldn't read a professional critic's score for this wine, so I've left that out.
- **[CellarTracker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CellarTracker) community: 90.1** (from your CellarTracker list).

**How it's drinking now.** In October 2026 the wine is ten years old, and your CellarTracker list gives a window of 2020 to 2028. So it is at its peak: drink it over the next year or two. Decant it for an hour, and serve at 16 to 18°C.

**Food.** A grilled ribeye, beef Wellington, or lamb chops with herbs.

**Value and where to buy.** BSW Liquor has Stags' Leap Winery's Napa Valley Cabernet 2021 at $54.99, the Petite Sirah 2018 at $46.99 and The Investor red blend 2020 at $84.99; ZYN has the Cabernet 2021 at $54.99 and the Petite Sirah 2018 at $48.50; BC Liquor has the Cabernet 2021 at $66.99.

**Curious details**
- **A resort before a winery.** For decades the estate was better known for hospitality than wine, under both the Chases and Frances Grange ([Dallas Wine Chick](https://www.dallaswinechick.com/sitting-down-with-christophe-paubert-a-winemaker-legend-from-stags-leap-winery/)).
